# Results — Study 914 (Securities-Lending Offset) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The measurement: for each pair
of same-asset-class ETFs, the **fee-adjusted relative tracking residual***

> `residual = annualised drift( log r_a − log r_b ) + (ER_a − ER_b)`

*i.e. the part of the realised return gap that the fee gap does **not** explain. Zero means
"fees explained everything"; positive means fund `a` delivered more than its fee
disadvantage implied — the signature the lending-offset claim predicts. Daily
**total-return** closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`) aggregated to month-end log
returns; HAC (Newey-West, 6 lags) *t*; 4,000-draw circular block bootstrap (6-month
blocks). As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current month is dropped).*

**Non-tape inputs, labelled.** Expense ratios are a **PROXY/ASSUMPTION** — the sponsors'
current published net ERs, held constant through history (`data.EXPENSE_RATIOS`). **This
assumption is one-sided and it decides the residual's sign**; the whole table is therefore
re-run below under early-era and time-averaged fee schedules, and that section is the one
to read before believing any headline here. Borrow fees in the tradable section are also an
**ASSUMPTION**, swept 0→100 bp/yr. Fund-level securities-lending revenue is **not public
tape at daily frequency** — everything here is an *inference from realised returns*, never a
read of the lending desk's books.

| **EEM − IEMG** | Emerging markets | 2012-11→2026-06 | 164 | −58.0 bp | +61.0 bp | **+3.0 bp/yr** | **+0.11** | [−50.1, +56.2] | 1.24% | 67 bp | 1.015 |
| **EFA − IEFA** | Developed ex-US | 2012-11→2026-06 | 164 | −21.4 bp | +26.0 bp | **+4.6 bp/yr** | **+0.24** | [−33.6, +43.4] | 0.82% | 44 bp | 0.993 |
| VEA − IEFA | Developed ex-US (cross-sponsor) | 2012-11→2026-06 | 164 | +52.7 bp | −4.0 bp | +48.7 bp/yr | +1.14 | [−25.1, +137.0] | 1.26% | 68 bp | 1.022 |
| IWM − IJR | US small cap | 2000-06→2026-06 | 313 | −127.3 bp | +13.0 bp | −114.3 bp/yr | −1.50 | [−264.3, +30.0] | 3.75% | 147 bp | 1.013 |

*Noise floor = the smallest annual effect this sample could resolve at |t| = 2, i.e.
2 × (tracking error / √years).*

- **On the three tight pairs the residual is 3 to 5 bp/yr with |*t*| ≤ 1.04.** The fee gap
  explains essentially the whole realised return gap. EEM's 58 bp/yr shortfall against IEMG
  is its 61 bp/yr fee disadvantage, to within 3 bp. **Read the fee-history sweep before
  reading anything into the *sign* of those 3–5 bp: it is smaller than the error in the fee
  assumption itself, and it flips.**
- **The two large residuals are composition, not lending.** IWM − IJR (−114 bp/yr) is the
  documented Russell-2000-vs-S&P-600 quality gap: those are different index families, and
  the residual is nowhere near the 13 bp fee gap it would have to be about. VEA − IEFA
  (+48.7 bp/yr) is FTSE-vs-MSCI country classification (Korea and Canada sit in VEA). Both
  are *below* their own noise floors in *t* terms.
- **The betas are all within 1.00 ± 0.03**, so these really are same-exposure pairs; the
  wedge is composition detail, not leverage.

## The structural control — the fund that legally cannot lend

**SPY is a unit investment trust**: by its 1993 structure it may not lend its securities.
**IVV is an open-end fund** that lends. Same index, same custodial universe, near-zero
composition wedge (TE 0.52%/yr, the tightest on the desk). If lending revenue reached
shareholders in a measurable way, IVV should beat SPY by *more* than the 6.5 bp/yr fee gap.

It does not. **The one number the tape delivers here is that SPY and IVV ran neck and neck:
SPY under-performed IVV by 1.4 bp/yr over 26 years, against a fee gap of between 0 and
6.5 bp/yr depending on which year's fee schedule you use.** Under today's published ERs
that is a residual of +5.1 bp/yr (*t* = +1.04, CI [−5.3, +15.1]); under the early-era
schedule, when IVV also charged 0.0945%, the same tape gives **−1.4 bp/yr** (*t* = −0.28).

**So the tape does not determine the sign of this residual — the fee assumption does.**
What survives either way is the magnitude: **any IVV lending advantage visible in returns is
within roughly ±5 bp/yr, and the 95% CI bounds it at ≈15 bp/yr.** That is the deliverable,
and it is well under what the marketing implies for a lending programme.

Two confounds sit inside this control and are *not* separable, so it bounds a **net**
quantity, not IVV's lending revenue alone: (i) SPY's UIT structure also forbids reinvesting
dividends between distributions (a cash drag that penalises SPY, pushing the residual
*down*), and (ii) SPY's own fee has been unchanged while IVV's fell fourfold. The control
answers "does IVV visibly out-earn SPY by more than fees?" — not "what does IVV's lending
desk make?"

## The fee-history sweep — the assumption that decides the sign

Every **cheap** leg on this desk had its fee cut hard during the sample (IVV 0.0945 → 0.03,
IEMG 0.18 → 0.09, IEFA 0.14 → 0.07, IJR 0.20 → 0.06) while the dear legs barely moved
(EEM 0.75 → 0.70, IWM 0.20 → 0.19, SPY unchanged). Pinning every fund at **today's** ER
therefore overstates every fee gap and biases every residual **upward** — in precisely the
direction that makes an offset look absent. Sweeping only the dear leg is a one-sided sweep.
So the whole table is re-run under three labelled fee scenarios (early-era / an approximate
time-weighted mid / today; `data.ER_HISTORY_BAND`, an ASSUMPTION reconstructed from
published cut schedules, not tape):

| Scenario | SPY−IVV | EEM−IEMG | EFA−IEFA | VEA−IEFA | IWM−IJR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Today's ERs (headline) | +5.1 bp | +3.0 bp | +4.6 bp | +48.7 bp | −114.3 bp |
| Approx. time-weighted | +2.1 bp | +0.0 bp | +3.1 bp | +49.7 bp | −122.8 bp |
| Earliest in-sample ERs (both legs) | +1.2 bp | −1.0 bp | −0.4 bp | +50.7 bp | −127.3 bp |

Sweeping the **cheap** leg alone (dear leg pinned at today's ER) is even starker — all three
tight-pair residuals cross zero:

| Pair | Cheap leg at its earliest in-sample ER | at mid | at today's ER |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY − IVV | −1.4 bp (*t* −0.28) | +1.6 bp (+0.32) | +5.1 bp (+1.04) |
| EEM − IEMG | −6.0 bp (*t* −0.22) | −1.0 bp (−0.03) | +3.0 bp (+0.11) |
| EFA − IEFA | −2.4 bp (*t* −0.13) | +2.6 bp (+0.13) | +4.6 bp (+0.24) |

**This is the study's most important robustness result and it cuts against the study's own
punchline.** The tight-pair residuals are *smaller than the uncertainty in the fee input*,
so the tape cannot say whether they are positive or negative. It can only say they are
**small**: |residual| ≲ 6 bp/yr on every same-sponsor pair under every fee scenario, with
|*t*| ≤ 1.04 throughout. Any claim that the residual comes out at "the wrong sign" for the
lending story is an artefact of pinning the cheap leg at its 2026 fee, and this study does
not make it.

## Pooling the tight pairs (the only way this tape gains power)

| Pool | Fee scenario | Window | n | Residual | HAC *t* | 95% CI | TE | Floor |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY−IVV, EEM−IEMG, EFA−IEFA | today's ERs | 2012-11→2026-06 | 164 | **+3.7 bp/yr** | **+0.31** | [−20.0, +27.2] | 0.55% | 30 bp |
| SPY−IVV, EEM−IEMG, EFA−IEFA | early-era ERs | 2012-11→2026-06 | 164 | **−0.6 bp/yr** | **−0.05** | [−24.3, +22.9] | 0.55% | 30 bp |
| All five pairs (incl. the two wedges) | today's ERs | 2012-11→2026-06 | 164 | +2.1 bp/yr | +0.08 | [−49.2, +53.3] | 0.87% | 47 bp |

Pooled, the answer is **zero under every fee scenario** (+3.7 bp/yr on today's fees, −0.6
bp/yr on early-era fees), with the CI bounding any systematic differential passthrough at
roughly **±25 bp/yr**. The all-five pool is shown so the class filter is visible rather than
convenient: dropping the two composition-wedge pairs is a *pre-stated* choice (different
index families, different sponsors), and it does not change the answer — it only tightens
the CI.

## Robustness

**Era cut (split 2020-01-01).**

| Pair | Early residual (*t*) | Late residual (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|
| SPY − IVV | +5.6 bp (+0.90) | +4.1 bp (+0.64) |
| EEM − IEMG | +14.9 bp (+0.58) | −6.8 bp (−0.13) |
| EFA − IEFA | −23.3 bp (−0.89) | +36.7 bp (+1.34) |
| VEA − IEFA | −16.2 bp (−0.67) | +125.8 bp (+1.55) |
| IWM − IJR | −159.3 bp (−2.06) | +6.5 bp (+0.03) |

Only SPY−IVV is stable across eras — and it is stable at *zero*. The only |*t*| > 2 anywhere
among the **residual** estimates (IWM−IJR, early era) is the small-cap **index quality gap**
flipping sign after 2020 — a fact about Russell versus S&P methodology, nothing to do with
fees or lending, and it points the *opposite* way to the lending story anyway. (The large
negative *t*'s in the trade table below are borrow costs being charged, not signal.)

**Expense-ratio assumption sweep, dear leg.** The residual moves one-for-one with the
assumed fee gap. This is the *smaller* half of the assumption — the cheap-leg sweep above is
the one that moves the sign:

| Pair | ER assumption | Fee gap | Residual | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| EEM − IEMG | 0.68% | +59.0 bp | +1.0 bp | +0.04 |
| EEM − IEMG | **0.70%** (headline) | +61.0 bp | +3.0 bp | +0.11 |
| EEM − IEMG | 0.72% | +63.0 bp | +5.0 bp | +0.18 |
| EEM − IEMG | 0.75% (the 2012 level) | +66.0 bp | +8.0 bp | +0.29 |
| EFA − IEFA | 0.32% / **0.33%** / 0.35% | +25 / +26 / +28 bp | +3.6 / +4.6 / +6.6 bp | +0.18 / +0.24 / +0.34 |
| IWM − IJR | 0.19% / 0.20% | +13 / +14 bp | −114.3 / −113.3 bp | −1.50 / −1.49 |

Across the whole plausible band the *magnitude* conclusion never moves: on every fee
scenario, dear leg or cheap leg, the tight pairs' residuals stay inside **±10 bp/yr** and
inside the noise. The *sign* does move, which is why this study reports a magnitude bound
and not a direction.

**Frequency check (daily instead of monthly).** Residuals +4.0, +4.0, +4.0, +47.7, −114.3
bp/yr for the five pairs (*t* = +0.29, +0.12, +0.18, +1.33, −1.49) — the same answer. Daily
tracking errors are 2–4× larger (SPY−IVV: 2.20% daily vs 0.52% monthly) because the two
funds pay dividends on different dates; that noise cancels within the month, which is why
the monthly series is the headline.

## The tradable leg — long the cheap fund, short the dear one

Dollar-neutral and **static** — the two tickers are fixed for the whole sample, so there is
**no signal and therefore no execution lag to apply; none is claimed**. The arithmetic
(`r_long − r_short`, month by month) is a book restored to equal notional at every month
end. Friction is charged once a year on the **full** notional of both legs (6 bp/yr, booked
in January, one period after the December book date — a cost convention, not a lag). That
charge is deliberately conservative: restoring equal notional only trades the legs' drift,
which on this tape is 1.0–9.5%/yr of notional, i.e. **0.03–0.29 bp/yr** at 3 bp one-way
against the **6.0 bp/yr** actually charged — the trade is charged 20–200× its true
rebalancing cost. Being dollar-neutral and self-financing, the book's return is already an
excess-of-cash quantity, so these Sharpes are directly comparable to any other excess-of-cash
Sharpe on the desk (with the standing caveat that a real short rebate lands *below* the cash
rate — which is what the borrow sweep is for).

| Trade | Borrow 0 bp | 25 bp | 50 bp | 100 bp |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **IEMG / EEM** | +47.0 bp, Sh +0.38, *t* +1.69 | +22.0 bp, +0.18 | **−3.0 bp, −0.02** | −53.0 bp, −0.43 |
| IEFA / EFA | +16.5 bp, Sh +0.20, *t* +0.85 | −8.5 bp, −0.10 | −33.5 bp, −0.41 | −83.5 bp, −1.02 |
| IVV / SPY | −5.2 bp, Sh −0.10 | −30.2 bp, −0.58 | −55.2 bp, −1.05 | −105.2 bp, −2.00 |
| IJR / IWM | +110.4 bp, Sh +0.29, *t* +1.45 | +85.4 bp, +0.23 | +60.4 bp, +0.16 | +10.4 bp, +0.03 |

Notice what is being harvested and what is not. **IEMG/EEM earns the 61 bp fee gap, not
lending revenue** — and it dies at roughly **50 bp/yr of borrow**, which is inside the range
an EM ETF actually borrows at. **IJR/IWM's +110 bp is the small-cap index quality premium**
(a different study's edge), with a 3.78% tracking error and *t* = +1.45 for its trouble.
Nothing here is a lending-revenue trade.

**Context — each leg's own excess-of-cash Sharpe (vs BIL, monthly):** EEM +0.26, IEMG +0.38,
IWM +0.43, IJR +0.47, SPY +0.64, IVV +0.64. The pair spreads above are one to two orders of
magnitude smaller than the assets they sit inside.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

On a *planted* world where the dearer fund is handed **+60 bp/yr** of lending passthrough,
the estimator recovers **+63.1 bp/yr** (error +3.1 bp) with *t* = **+4.89**. On the null
(fees and composition noise only) it returns **+2.7 bp/yr on average across 8 seeds** (sd
13.9 bp) and fires |*t*| ≥ 2 on **0/8**. Pooling five planted pairs recovers **+64.7 bp**
with *t* = **+10.37**. The estimator is unbiased and *is* powerful enough to see a 60 bp
effect — so the real-tape zero is a property of the tape, not of the harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The claim that lending revenue systematically makes realised tracking
  difference *better* than −ER does not show up in returns. On the three tight pairs the
  fee-adjusted residual is **+3.0 / +4.6 / +5.1 bp/yr** with |*t*| ≤ 1.04 and CIs straddling
  zero; pooled it is **+3.7 bp/yr (*t* = +0.31)**, and **−0.6 bp/yr (*t* = −0.05)** if the
  funds are charged their early-era fees instead. The two headline-sized residuals
  (IWM−IJR −114 bp, VEA−IEFA +49 bp) are **index-composition wedges**, not fee or lending
  effects, and neither clears |*t*| = 2 over the full sample. Four honest caveats sit on
  this axis: (i) **power** — a same-class pair's tracking error (0.5–3.8%/yr) sets a noise
  floor of 20–147 bp/yr, while a realistic net lending yield for these funds is 1–15 bp/yr,
  so the tape can *bound* the effect but could never have resolved it at its true size;
  (ii) **the fee assumption owns the sign** — every cheap leg's ER was cut during the
  sample, so pinning it at today's value inflates each residual by roughly its own size.
  Sweep the cheap leg back to its earliest in-sample fee and all three tight-pair residuals
  turn negative (**−1.4 / −6.0 / −2.4 bp/yr**); charge *both* legs their earliest fees and
  they sit at **+1.2 / −1.0 / −0.4 bp/yr**. Either way they are zero, and the sign is the
  assumption's, not the tape's. The study therefore reports a **magnitude bound only** and
  makes no claim about direction;
  (iii) the SPY/IVV control **confounds** the lending asymmetry with SPY's UIT dividend
  cash drag and with its unchanged fee, so it bounds a *net* structural difference, not
  IVV's lending revenue; (iv) **fund survivorship** — all ten funds here are survivors,
  chosen because they still trade, so the sample is tilted toward well-run products.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** There is no lending-revenue spread to bank. What is bankable is
  the **fee gap itself**, and it is thin: IEMG/EEM earns +47 bp/yr gross, +22 bp at 25 bp
  borrow, and **−3 bp at 50 bp borrow** — inside the range EM ETF borrow actually costs. The
  IJR/IWM spread that does pay (+110 bp/yr) is the small-cap index quality premium wearing a
  3.78% tracking error and *t* = +1.45, not a lending trade. The practical conclusion is the
  boring one: if you want the cheap fund's return, **own the cheap fund** — do not try to
  short the dear one to capture the difference.
- **What the study actually delivers.** Not an estimate, not a sign, but a **magnitude
  bound**: whatever the lending desks earn, and however much of it is credited back, the
  amount that reaches the shareholder as measurable *relative* return is smaller than
  ≈6 bp/yr on every same-sponsor pair under every fee scenario (CI edge ≈15 bp/yr on the
  tightest pair, ≈25 bp/yr pooled). The offset is real in the sponsors' annual reports; at
  the size it plausibly has, it is **invisible in the tape** — and this tape was never
  capable of resolving it either way.
